cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator pointed out that the fixture path still named the old worktree
cases.why: Pointing out an error in the agent's work is a correction.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; operator clarified that the budget is counted per order, not per session
cases.why: Clarifying what was meant is a correction.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator rejected the new retry dependency and asked for a plain loop
cases.why: The first step is a rejection; the request that follows it comes second and does not set the class.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator objected to swallowing the hook error silently
cases.why: Objecting to the agent's approach rejects it, which is a correction.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; operator correction: the heading names the order, not the branch
cases.why: An explicitly named operator correction.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator refined criterion 3 so it counts only merged orders
cases.why: Refining what a criterion meant is a correction, not a new direction.

cases.dispatch: Operator corrected the executor: the refusal count is five, not four
cases.why: Old free-text record in which the operator corrects the agent.

cases.dispatch: resume: final review; the operator overruled the reviewer's plan to squash the branch history
cases.why: Overruling the agent's plan rejects it; no hold or gate was overridden, so it is not override.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the reviewer requested a rename; the operator objected and kept the old name
cases.why: The reviewer's request is another actor's act; the first operator step is an objection.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; continued under the operator's standing no-new-deps rule; the operator pointed out the lockfile still changed
cases.why: Continued under and standing make the rule a reference; the first live step points out an error.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; no override was needed; the operator pointed out the gate was reading a stale cache
cases.why: The negated override is not a step; pointing out the stale cache is the first step.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator said the synthesis misread the intake and restated the goal
cases.why: Saying the agent misread and restating the goal corrects it even without a keyword.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator asked for a --dry-run flag before any write path lands
cases.why: Asked for is a request, not a question.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator told the executor to drop the retry loop and fail fast
cases.why: Told the executor to is an instruction.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator required that setup must not require network access
cases.why: Required is the step; the modal must not require is only its content.

cases.dispatch: resume: final review; the operator approved publishing without a changelog entry
cases.why: An approval on the operator's own initiative; no agent question is named.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; operator signed off on splitting the migration into two commits
cases.why: Signed off is an unprompted approval.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator permitted one extra fixture directory under test/
cases.why: Permitting something is direction.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; operator directed that audit output stay byte-identical to the console
cases.why: Directed is direction.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator steered the repair toward the parser rather than the test
cases.why: Steering the work is direction.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; no operator correction was needed; the operator requested a changelog line
cases.why: The negated correction is not a step; the first real step is a request.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator rejected the retry loop (D003), then asked for a timeout flag
cases.why: The D003 citation makes the rejection a reference; the first live step is a request.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; after the verifier's finding, the operator instructed a rerun on a clean cache
cases.why: After attaches to the verifier's finding, not to an operator step, so the instruction is live.

cases.dispatch: Operator resume: next; operator authorized adding one dev dependency for the fuzzer
cases.why: The old-style label is not a step; authorizing a dependency, not an override, is direction.

cases.dispatch: scope expand: WO-181 also covers the Codex compaction adapter
cases.why: A leading scope expand: prefix is the first step.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator widened WO-190 to include the audit route
cases.why: Widening the order is a scope expansion.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; operator added the Windows path bug to this order's scope
cases.why: Adding work to the order's scope expands it.

cases.dispatch: scope expand: fold the console export into WO-177; the operator also asked for one PR
cases.why: The leading prefix is the first step; the later request does not change the class.

cases.dispatch: Operator expanded WO-066 to also rewrite the budget table
cases.why: Old free-text record of the operator expanding the order.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; within the operator's standing budget, the operator expanded the order to cover old receipts
cases.why: Within and standing make the budget a reference; the first live step expands scope.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator brought the flaky timer test into this order's scope
cases.why: Bringing new work into the order expands its scope.

cases.dispatch: operator override: cleared the writer reservation left by a crashed session
cases.why: A leading operator override: prefix is the first step.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator authorized an override of the subagent cap for this run
cases.why: Authorizing an override is override, not direction.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator overrode the planning-branch hold to land one script fix
cases.why: Overriding a hold is override.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator overruled the stale writer hold so the repair could commit
cases.why: Overruling a hold overrides it.

cases.dispatch: operator override: restore the success record; the operator then clarified the rerun order
cases.why: The leading prefix is the first step; the later clarification does not set the class.

cases.dispatch: resume: verify; the operator invoked operator override: to stop a gate stuck on a dead worker
cases.why: A live, unmarked use of operator override after the dispatch label.

cases.dispatch: Operator used an override to lift the npm-test write refusal and repair a corrupted record
cases.why: Old free-text record of the operator using an override.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator did not correct the patch but lifted the evidence hold by override
cases.why: The negated correction is not a step; lifting a hold by override is.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the session died mid-rebase and the operator took over to finish the merge
cases.why: The operator took over a failed session.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the executor hung on a hook; the operator stepped in and completed the handoff by hand
cases.why: The executor's hang is not an operator step; stepping in on the stopped session is a takeover.

cases.dispatch: resume: verify; operator takeover of the verifier session after it failed on a context limit
cases.why: Noun-form takeover; after attaches to the failure, not to a prior operator step.

cases.dispatch: Operator took over the stalled executor run and committed the fix directly
cases.why: Old free-text record of a takeover of a stalled session.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator picked up the failed session and reran the gate from its last step
cases.why: Picking up a failed session is a takeover, not a picked option.

cases.dispatch: resume: final review; the reviewer session failed at publish and the operator took it over to cut the tag
cases.why: The reviewer's failure is not an operator step; taking over the failed session is.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the executor asked which lock layout to keep; the operator chose the flat file
cases.why: The executor's question is not an operator step; choosing in reply is an answer.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; operator picked option 2: keep the old flag as an alias
cases.why: Picking an offered option is an answer.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; operator response: yes, keep both receipts
cases.why: An operator response to the agent's question.

cases.dispatch: resume: final review; when the reviewer asked about signing, the operator replied that the tag stays unsigned
cases.why: A reply to a question the agent put.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator confirmed the branch name the executor proposed
cases.why: Confirming a choice the agent put is an answer, not an approval.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the executor offered three repair paths and the operator went with rerunning from a clean cache
cases.why: Went with one of the offered paths means the operator chose an option.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; operator answered the executor's question: the cap is per order
cases.why: Answered the agent's question.

cases.dispatch: resume: verify; the operator selected 'Accept with finding' when the verifier asked how to file
cases.why: Selected an option the verifier put; this is not a model selection.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; Keep both receipts (Recommended)
cases.why: A bare picked option label; the Recommended tag marks an offered choice.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; continued under the operator's standing budget (D004); when the executor asked about the flaky test, the operator chose to quarantine it
cases.why: The standing, cited budget is a reference; the first live step answers the agent's question.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator asked why the verify gate took forty minutes
cases.why: A question (asked why), not a request (asked for).

cases.dispatch: resume: next; operator note: CI runners are offline until Monday
cases.why: A note is an operator step outside the six.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator sent ideation messages about audit retention mid-run
cases.why: Ideation messages are other-step.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the operator ran the installer live on a fresh laptop and it stopped at step 3
cases.why: A live attempt the operator ran.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator reported that the hosted runner queue was backed up for an hour
cases.why: A report of an observation; it corrects nothing the agent did.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the executor answered the operator's question about why the lock outlived the session
cases.why: The executor's answer is not an operator step; the operator's unmarked question is the first step.

cases.dispatch: resume: verify; the operator asked whether VER-171-2 supersedes VER-171-1
cases.why: A question asked by the operator.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator mused about moving budgets into the store; no change was requested
cases.why: Musing is ideation; the negated request after it is not a step.

cases.dispatch: resume: verify
cases.why: The dispatch label alone names no operator step.

cases.dispatch: Operator resume: fix; fixed both findings from VER-058-1 and reran the gate
cases.why: Operator is part of the old-style label and fix is executor work; no operator step.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; addressed the Operator direction section of VER-172-1
cases.why: Operator direction is a section title here, not a step.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; ran at the model and effort the operator selected for the order
cases.why: A model the operator selected is not a step.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator selected Sonnet at medium effort for this order
cases.why: A model selection is none even though selected is an answer verb.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; continued under the operator's standing instruction to keep commits small
cases.why: Continued under and standing make the instruction a reference.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; worked within the scope the operator expanded in D003
cases.why: Within and the D003 citation make the expansion a reference.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; the verifier rejected the evidence table and the executor corrected it before rerunning
cases.why: Rejection and correction by the verifier and executor are not operator steps.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the CLI must not require a login, and the operator must be able to run it offline
cases.why: Modal requirements; the mention of the operator is not a step.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; no operator correction was needed
cases.why: A negated step is not a step.

cases.dispatch: resume: final review; the operator did not approve a retag, so the existing tag stands
cases.why: A negated approval is not a step.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; continued after the operator's takeover of the failed session
cases.why: Continued after marks the takeover as prior.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator required a dry-run flag (WO-151-D004); the executor implemented it
cases.why: The decision reference after the step marks it cited; the executor act is not an operator step.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; open question for the operator: should the old flag stay as an alias?
cases.why: A question put to the operator, not one the operator asked; no step yet.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; the operator's standing default of high effort applied to every phase
cases.why: A standing default is a reference, not a step.

cases.dispatch: resume: next; a subagent picked the cheaper fixture set, then the executor took over its checks
cases.why: Picked and took over are acts of a subagent and the executor, not the operator.

cases.dispatch: resume: fix; applied the operator's correction as recorded in the WO-160 decisions
cases.why: Recorded marks the correction as cited.
